messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (varies by county).
• In cities: 35–45 mph (often 25 mph in school zones). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or weighing <80 lb must be in a child safety seat. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system). | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for adults; lower limits for commercial drivers and those under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles on the right yield to those on the left. | | **School Bus Regulations** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is generally prohibited. | | **Parking Restrictions** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant, crosswalk, or intersection. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights mean stop; yellow means prepare to stop unless it’s unsafe. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must have valid registration and pass annual safety inspections. | For detailed statutes, consult the Texas Transportation Code or the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles website.
